The two-step BDRS derivative has mode polynomial lambda²-2sigma lambda+sigma and spectral radius s2<1. Analyticity plus an adapted norm proves a local basin with any rate above s2; the coupling-output derivative is nonzero on each positive top mode, proving sharpness. The exact-rational script verifies the recurrence, feasibility and exemplars, while finite differences check derivative numerically. No experimental step is used for the universal proof.

value.rationale: A rigorous unconditional local-attraction boundary is meaningful because the same 2026 BDRS-MS algorithm has explicit strictly positive globally periodic trajectories; the result reconciles the local and global behaviors rather than repairing an old source. The exact s2-versus-s2² comparison proves that log-momentum BDRS is locally slower than ordinary Sinkhorn and can be arbitrarily slow, identifying an algorithm-design tradeoff invisible in the earlier projective-diameter sufficient condition. The claim is an all-dimensions structural theorem with sharp two-dimensional witnesses, not a routine special-case computation.
